themes.storage: localStorage key "mh-theme" holds "light" or "dark"; absent means system.
themes.application: Inline head script sets data-theme on <html> before first paint. Tokens live in :root (light), :root[data-theme="dark"], and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme="light"]). Frontmatter keys ending in -dark are the dark values of the same role.

display.purpose: Hero headline only; 2.35rem on phones; max 14ch.

headline.purpose: Section titles, always under the 3px ink section rule.

title.purpose: Part, project, step-panel, step and form titles (1.05 to 2.4rem); demo headings at 1.25rem, 105% width.

number.purpose: Part, step, callout and chip numbers, module keys A to D, carousel dots; normal width, sized to the circle.

label.purpose: Buttons, chips, pills, tabs, nav links, form labels; sentence case.

caption.purpose: Fig. captions, hints, demo notes, legends, footer, in Ink Muted.

shadows.name: shadow-color
shadows.purpose: One shadow color per theme. Dark: rgba(2, 8, 24, 0.7). Light: intended navy ink; the build currently declares it as a self-reference (invalid), see drift.

shadows.name: stage-lift
shadows.purpose: Browser demo frame; -32px spread on the step panel.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Input focus with the border turned Assembly Blue; 6px on the current step circle.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button, chip, pill, tab, link and input state changes.

motion.name: theme-change
motion.purpose: Body background and text color when the theme switches.

motion.name: piece-travel
motion.purpose: Exploded-view pieces and callouts moving along their guides on load and on selection.

motion.name: demo-in
motion.purpose: Entering demo panels, option steps, product cards and the step-panel text.

motion.name: assembly-stage
motion.purpose: Progressive assembly drawing moving between stages.

motion.name: tour
motion.purpose: Reader-started step tour; stops at the last step or on any interaction.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Replaces piece travel, demo entrances, slide and fill transitions, and smooth scroll.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a printed assembly manual. White paper carries a faint blue 24px grid. Every object is a single-weight blue line drawing, every part has a number in a circle, and dotted guide lines with arrowheads show where each piece goes. Navy ink sets the text. MH does the assembling, and the page shows the parts, working demonstrations of them, the finished builds and the numbered steps.

The manual has two printings. The light theme is the printed manual: navy ink on white paper. The dark theme is the blueprint, a cyanotype: pale ink and pale blue line on deep blue paper with a pale grid. Both themes use the same roles and the same drawings, and only the token values change. The reader picks light, dark or system, and system is the default.

Density is calm and orderly. Sections open on a heavy ink rule like the heading of a manual page. Lists are bounded sheets divided by dashed cut lines. Real project screenshots sit in thin ink frames with "Fig. n" captions. Interactive demos sit in a line-drawn browser frame marked as a demonstration. Color does nothing decorative: blue marks what is drawn, what is selected and what you can act on, and nothing else. The world rejects the generic agency landing page (split hero with a screen mockup, then a grid of icon cards).

Motion follows the manual. On load, the exploded-view pieces slide in along their guides once. Choosing a piece fills it and moves it toward its place on the notebook while the others turn dashed. Stepping through the instructions fills the step rail and assembles the drawing stage by stage. Nothing moves on its own except a guided tour the reader starts, which runs once and stops.
keyCharacteristics: Two printings of one manual: white paper with navy ink, or blueprint paper with pale ink.
Single-weight blue line drawing for every object and icon.
Part numbers and keys in circles, set in Archivo.
Dotted guide lines and arrows to show sequence and placement.
A strict state vocabulary: selected, available, dimmed.
Expanded Archivo headings over Hanken Grotesk text.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means drawn, chosen or actionable. It never appears as a background wash, a gradient or decoration.

rules.name: The Ink Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every gray is the ink at reduced strength (Ink, Ink Soft, Ink Muted, Rule, Field Line): navy on light paper, pale blue on blueprint paper. Do not use neutral or warm grays.

rules.name: The Same Roles Rule
rules.body: A theme changes token values, never roles. Components read only the role tokens, so every component, drawing and state works in both printings without a per-theme override.

rules.name: The Stamped Heading Rule
rules.body: Every h1 to h3 is Archivo 800 at 112% width with balanced wrapping. Body text never uses Archivo.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no tracked-out small caps, and no kicker lines above headings. Each section opens with its heading directly under the rule.

rules.name: The Line First Rule
rules.body: A border separates things before a shadow does. Only the five roles above get shadows. The parts list, chips, pills, tabs, round buttons, option cards, product cards, tags and nav stay flat.

rules.name: The Three States Rule
rules.body: Selected = Selection Wash fill plus a heavy Assembly Blue line (a 3px effective border on chips, pills, tabs and option cards; a 3.5px stroke on drawn pieces). Available = line only, with no fill change. Dimmed or unavailable = dashed line, muted ink (40% opacity on drawn pieces, struck-through text on unavailable pills). No other state treatment exists.

rules.name: The Selected Number Rule
rules.body: A circle that marks a part or a choice is line-only at rest. When its item is selected, the circle fills solid Assembly Blue with On Blue content: chip numbers and callouts, module keys, the current step, the current carousel dot and the pressed theme button. Steps already passed keep a blue line without a fill. This fill is the selected state applied to the circle, not a badge.

rules.name: The Circled Number Rule
rules.body: Part, step, callout and key numbers always sit in circles in Archivo 800 at 100% width. The number marks a part.

dos: Do draw every object as a single-weight Assembly Blue line with round caps (2px detail, 2.5px outline).
Do read only role tokens in components, so each one works in the printed and blueprint themes without overrides.
Do use exactly three states: Selection Wash fill plus heavy blue line for selected, line only for available, dashed and muted for dimmed or unavailable.
Do put part, step and key numbers in circles in Archivo 800 at 100% width, filling the circle solid blue only when its item is selected.
Do open every section with a 3px Ink top rule followed directly by the Archivo headline.
Do separate rows inside a sheet with 1.5px dashed Rule cut lines, and keep sheet borders at 1.5px solid Ink.
Do caption real project screenshots and the assembly drawing as "Fig. n · description".
Do put interactive demos inside the line-drawn browser frame with its "Demostración" tag.
Do let motion follow the guides: pieces arrive along their dotted lines once on load, and nothing advances or loops on its own.
donts: Don't add uppercase kickers or eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't fill shapes with Assembly Blue to show emphasis. Solid blue is reserved for the primary action, outline-action hover, selected circles and toggles, the step rail fill and the compare handle.
Don't use filled, duotone or glyph icons. Icons are inline SVG line drawings at 1.8 to 2 stroke, except the WhatsApp brand mark.
Don't use hard offset shadows or add shadows beyond the action, plate, sheet, stage and handle roles.
Don't use dashed lines for anything that is selected or active. Dashed means guide, cut line, not yet done, or dimmed.
Don't give a theme its own colors for a role, or its own component styles. Change the token value, never the role.
Don't build the split hero with a screen mockup followed by a grid of icon cards.
